items.title: Mrs. Francis Oliver Interview, 1969-05-10
items.q: I worked in a place they used to call it Bucktown... And he played it for special parties

ctx.x: Garden parties, things in the backyard all the time. And I mean, on holidays and like First of July and Labor Day and things like that, we'd have the whole family together. Looked like my grandmother was sitting up there like the queen, all her kids would come in. She expected them, and it didn't disappoint her either.
There weren't so many piano players down here. I guess a lot of those bands didn't use piano, but... Well, no, because Piran was a violinist, you know.

He played violin. Yes. And he really played. He's old. I worked at a place after I came back from Chicago, because I was going to school in the daytime, and I'd have to work at evening because I had to support my kids, you know, my son. And I worked in a place they used to call it Bucktown. Oh, yes, out by the lake. And he played it for special parties, you know, dinner parties. It was really and truly a supper club.
